findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and will raise TypeError when instantiated
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed to subclass `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass` as a body. `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares four abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`), none of which are implemented here, so the class remains abstract. `Detector.detector_handler` instantiates the registered handler via `group_type.detector_handler(self)`; for any detector of type `metric_alert_fire` this now raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler ...` instead of returning a handler (previously it returned a no-op handler whose `evaluate` returned an empty list). Any code path that resolves the handler for a metric alert detector will crash rather than no-op. Either implement the abstract methods (even as stubs raising NotImplementedError only when actually called) or keep it on the non-abstract base until the real implementation lands.

findings.title: get_state_data raises KeyError when counter_names is empty
findings.body: In `get_state_data`, `counter_updates` is initialized to `{}` and only populated inside `if self.counter_names:`. The result loop then unconditionally does `counter_updates=counter_updates[gk]`, which raises `KeyError` for every group key when a subclass legitimately declares `counter_names = []`. With the new `StatefulDetectorHandler` hook being the intended base for real detectors (e.g. metric alerts, which may not need counters), this will blow up during evaluation. Use `counter_updates.get(gk, {})` or build a default dict of `{name: None}` per group key.

findings.title: Docstring still says evaluate returns a list
findings.body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` now returns `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but its docstring still reads "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`. There will be one result for each group key result in the packet". This misdescribes the return contract for implementers/callers; update it to describe the dict keyed by group key.

findings.title: Stale TODO comment about stateful detector
findings.body: The comment `# TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction` sits directly above a class that now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler`, so the TODO is already satisfied and is misleading. It should be removed or replaced with the remaining work (implementing the abstract hooks).

findings.title: Multi-group test builds expected occurrence with the wrong value
findings.body: `test_state_results_multi_group` sends `{"group_1": 6, "group_2": 10}` but constructs the expected occurrence for `group_2` with `value=6` (`build_mock_occurrence_and_event(detector.detector_handler, "group_2", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)`). The assertion only passes because the mock builder ignores the `value` argument entirely, so the test does not verify that `evaluate_group_key_value` passes the correct group value into `build_occurrence_and_event_data` — a regression in that argument would go undetected. Either pass 10 and make the mock occurrence depend on `value` (e.g. in `evidence_data`), or assert on the hook arguments directly.
